title: GETS: Generalized Ensemble Temperature Scaling for NBA Probability Calibration
hypothesis: GETS replaces scalar temperature T with an ensemble of K temperatures {T1,...,TK}, each learned on a different validation fold. Final calibrated probability is a weighted average over ensemble members. This is empirically superior to: (a) single temperature scaling, (b) isotonic regression (which overfits on small sports datasets), and (c) Platt/sigmoid calibration. ICLR 2025 reports ECE reduction of ~0.008-0.015 on tabular classification vs isotonic baseline.

phase_1.description: Add GETS as new calibration method 'gets' in hf-space/app.py
phase_1.code_sketch:
if cal_method == 'gets':
    m.fit(X_sub[ti_safe], y_eval[ti_safe])
    _model_fitted = True
    K = 5  # ensemble size
    fold_size = max(50, len(ti_safe) // K)
    temps = []
    from scipy.optimize import minimize_scalar
    for k in range(K):
        cal_slice = ti_safe[-(k+1)*fold_size : -k*fold_size if k > 0 else len(ti_safe)]
        if len(cal_slice) < 20: continue
        raw_p = np.clip(m.predict_proba(X_sub[cal_slice])[:, 1], 1e-6, 1-1e-6)
        logits = np.log(raw_p / (1 - raw_p))
        def brier_loss(t):
            p_cal = 1 / (1 + np.exp(-logits / t))
            return np.mean((p_cal - y_eval[cal_slice])**2)
        res = minimize_scalar(brier_loss, bounds=(0.1, 5.0), method='bounded')
        temps.append(res.x)
    _gets_temps = temps if temps else None
    cal_method = 'none'

advantages_over_current.vs_beta: GETS adapts temperature per fold (temporal robustness), BetaCalibration fits on single held-out slice
advantages_over_current.vs_isotonic: GETS never overfits — temperature is a single scalar per fold (1 param vs N for isotonic)
advantages_over_current.vs_lr_meta: GETS uses logit-space temperature (theoretically grounded) vs linear prob-space LR
advantages_over_current.vs_venn_abers: GETS has no external MAPIE dependency, simpler, faster

deps_needed: scipy.optimize.minimize_scalar (already in scipy, installed on HF spaces)

alternative_technique.name: ATS-CP: Adaptive Temperature Scaling + Conformal Prediction
alternative_technique.description: Combines temperature scaling with conformal coverage guarantees. For each test game, outputs a prediction interval [p_low, p_high] with 90% coverage. Use as risk management overlay on Kelly sizing.
alternative_technique.implementation_complexity: MEDIUM — requires calibration holdout + conformal quantile computation

related_finding.title: Load Management 8-Feature Block (CMU, Spring 2025)
related_finding.description: CMU capstone found 8 features predict load management decisions with AUC 0.81: player_age, season_minutes_rate, games_played_7d, rest_days_before_game, back_to_back_flag, road_games_streak, fatigue_index (custom), team_playoff_odds. These can be added as Cat50 expansion features to engine.py.
